claims.wording: Clean My Ubuntu is HomieLab's independent Ubuntu cleanup project; cmu is its terminal app/command.
claims.excerpt: It's a desktop app and a terminal app (cmu) that share one engine. ... MIT © 2026 HomieLab ... Clean My Ubuntu is an independent open-source project, not affiliated with MacPaw or CleanMyMac.
claims.conditions: Not a PowerMyMac alias claim; no exhaustive all-brand alias search asserted.

claims.wording: The desktop app requires Ubuntu 24.04+; Ubuntu 22.04 uses the terminal app from the app grid.
claims.excerpt: On Ubuntu 22.04 the app grid opens the terminal app (the desktop app needs 24.04+).
claims.conditions: Do not expand into certified support for all Linux distributions or macOS/Windows. Architectures not verified.

claims.wording: It is free and MIT-licensed; the optional Ko-fi contribution is not a verified paid tier.
claims.excerpt: Clean My Ubuntu is free and always will be. If it saved you some space (or some time), you can buy me a coffee on Ko-fi ... License MIT
claims.conditions: Publisher offer, not purchase test or guarantee of future terms; no invented currency or subscription.

claims.wording: Normal desktop cleanup is Scan, deselect items to keep, then Clean; locked items use Ubuntu's password dialog.
claims.excerpt: press Scan, untick anything you want to keep, press Clean. Items with a 🔒 need your password (the standard Ubuntu dialog); everything else runs as you.
claims.conditions: Not an unconditional confirmation guarantee: documented --clean --yes and automatic cleaning can run without an interactive confirmation.

claims.wording: Documented developer targets include npm, pnpm, pip, Go, Cargo and Docker; downloaded AI models are separate choices, never preselected or automatically cleaned.
claims.excerpt: npm, Yarn, pnpm, Bun, pip, Go, Cargo, Gradle, Maven, Conda; Docker images, build cache, containers and volumes (each separately) ... each Ollama, Hugging Face and LM Studio model on its own — never pre-selected, never cleaned automatically
claims.conditions: Do not equate models, logs, histories, volumes and caches; no universal disposable-data claim or measured speed.

claims.wording: The terminal app documents folder-size browsing, duplicates, uninstalling and a system overview with free-space history.
claims.excerpt: More tools in the terminal app: Uninstaller ... System Overview — storage, free-space history ... Space Lens (browse folders by size), Large & Old Files ... Duplicates, Startup Items and Settings.
claims.conditions: Do not attribute all these tools to the GTK desktop UI or claim Breathing Room has matching tools.

claims.wording: Automatic cleaning is documented with daily, weekly or monthly scheduling and limited targets; it does not automatically empty Trash or clean browsers/apps.
claims.excerpt: runs a weekly (or daily, monthly) clean of user and developer junk ... It never empties the Trash, never touches browsers or apps, never needs your password
claims.conditions: Documented systemd user timer, not tested execution. Notification numbers in README are examples.

claims.wording: The publisher says scanning and cleaning records stay local, while update checks/downloads contact GitHub and system maintenance tools may go online.
claims.excerpt: scan results, sizes and file lists are shown to you and never sent anywhere ... Once a day while you use the app ... Reads the latest version number from raw.githubusercontent.com ... Never happens when installed as a package. ... Like any web request, GitHub sees your IP address ... Maintenance → Update everything runs apt update.
claims.conditions: Do not promise zero network use or independently audited privacy.

workflow.proposedTitle: Moving an Ubuntu developer cleanup workflow to a Mac
workflow.primaryIntent: A Clean My Ubuntu user switching to macOS needs to separate reusable package caches from models, app data and system-specific maintenance.
workflow.descriptionDirection: Keep the review-first habit, not Ubuntu's system commands. Explain how to inspect a Mac's storage and decide what can be rebuilt before choosing any cleanup action.
outline: Answer first: migrate the decision process, not APT/Snap/journal commands; disclose we build Breathing Room.
Show official Clean My Ubuntu Smart Scan visual and label publisher numbers as untested.
Map categories: package caches, old logs, downloaded models, Docker volumes and personal/project data; do not treat these as interchangeable junk.
Inspect storage owners and folder context in the Mac preview; show Space with example-data disclosures.
Build a keep/rebuild/review checklist: who owns it, can it be regenerated, what download cost, what data would be lost, and which approval applies?
State platform, Python, preview signing, paid hosted AI and scheduled-runtime boundaries; recommend neither app for an unsupported OS.
Link comparison/hub and any existing tested tool only after routes are verified.

comparison.proposedTitle: Clean My Ubuntu and Breathing Room: choosing for your operating system
comparison.primaryIntent: Concise platform-first decision for an Ubuntu user now using a Mac, not two apps competing on one OS.
comparison.conclusion: For Ubuntu, Clean My Ubuntu documents Ubuntu-native package/log and terminal workflows. For a Mac, consider Breathing Room, which we build, only if its preview, Python and hosted-AI conditions fit. These are not interchangeable installers.
comparison.length: Concise; do not expand the matrix into a duplicate workflow post.

briefs.interactionPass: Hand off a static platform-first decision aid: Ubuntu → official Ubuntu utility docs; Mac → inspect/rebuild/review checklist and preview caveats; other OS → no verified recommendation. Then classify a candidate as regenerable cache, retained model/data, or unknown requiring owner review. No deletion, upload or invented numeric estimator.

competitor: Free MIT project with documented desktop and terminal workflows on Ubuntu.
Ubuntu package/system targets plus additional terminal uninstaller/duplicates tools.
Documented local processing and no-account policy, qualified by network exceptions.
Documented scheduling and free-space history; do not imply Breathing Room alone offers recurrence.
breathingRoom: Mac-oriented storage inspection, grouped helpers and sampled activity source implementations; fit for the Mac side of a migration, not an Ubuntu replacement binary.
Documented constrained native cleanup and saved-approval design, with narrow automatic Ruff exception disclosed.
tradeoffs: Competitor macOS support is not verified; Ubuntu commands are not Mac instructions.
Breathing Room is a non-notarized preview requiring Python 3.10+; physical Intel and clean-machine validation remain pending.
Breathing Room hosted assistant needs authentication/network; optional AI Care is recurring paid service, unlike competitor's advertised free local utility.
No comparative speed, safety, space-recovered or hands-on outcome claims supported.
